title: Pass 5 mints near-duplicate activity entities (exact-match get_or_create, no fuzzy/semantic dedup)
description: Surfaced by the clean-by-construction smoke run (epic 27w, acceptance c): a 6-concept seed (Wall/Window/Roof/Concrete/Corridor/Concrete Pouring) produced 561 activity entities, ALL with literally-distinct names (count(*) == count(DISTINCT lower(name)) == 561) but heavy SEMANTIC redundancy. Distinct from yms (which correctly declined to BOUND the activity count -- these are legitimate construction activities, not junk) and from 8tk (pattern quota-padding). This is an entity-level dedup gap that dilutes the activity layer / process graph. OPTIONS: (a) embedding/fuzzy match in get_or_create against existing activities before minting; (b) a pass-2-style clustering/merge pass scoped to activities; (c) canonicalize activity names. Measure redundancy precisely first.
notes: STRATEGY 2026-06-28: production will be REBUILT, not repaired in place. This is the one item that is NOT a data artifact — it is a pipeline DEFECT that REPRODUCES in a fresh run (the smoke run minted 561 near-dup activities from 6 seeds).   bsos extract --passes 10 --models deepseek-chat   # --models needed for 10b LLM disambiguation

description:

There is no tool that maps from an IFC element description to relevant bsos entities. Without this, the agent must guess entity names and the whole query chain is fragile.

Add a bsos MCP tool (e.g. search_entities) that accepts a free-text description or IFC class name and returns ranked matching bsos entities. Semantic similarity (embedding-based) is the right approach given entity names may not literally match IFC names. This is the bridge between the two systems and is the most critical gap for agent usability.

title: abstraction_node_effective_origins SQLite view
description:
Create the required SQLite view abstraction_node_effective_origins (Section 4.8, Section 12).

The view computes majority knowledge_origin for AbstractionNode records via GROUP BY + aggregation over child assertions. Required because any query filtering or sorting AbstractionNode by knowledge_origin MUST join against this view — it cannot be bypassed by call sites.

bsos init MUST create this view alongside Alembic-managed tables. bsos doctor MUST verify its existence and fail loudly if missing.

SQL sketch:
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS abstraction_node_effective_origins AS
  SELECT an.id AS node_id,
         a.knowledge_origin,
         COUNT(*) AS origin_count
  FROM abstraction_nodes an
  JOIN assertions a ON a.id IN (json_each(an.assertion_ids))
  GROUP BY an.id, a.knowledge_origin;

title: process_relations: generic hub entities conflate context-specific sequences into false cycles
description:
Discovered while working building_domain-g3r (resolving the 432 cycle-conflicted
process_relations from building_domain-8lp's cycle detector). Of the 16 SCCs,
12 small ones (24 edges) were genuine extraction bugs (a reverse edge actually
described a distinct later step — "second layer"/"next course"/"opposite side"/
"above" — that never got its own entity, so it reused the earlier-phase entity
and created a false 2-edge cycle) and were resolved directly.

The remaining 4 groups (408 edges: one 384-edge/198-node cluster, plus 17/3/4-edge
groups covering interior-finish trades, envelope sequencing, and parking-lot
amenities) are a different, harder problem: process_relations has no way to
scope an ordering to a building type, structural system, or method variant.
Generic canonical activities — e.g. "Foundation Construction" (31 outgoing
edges, 1 incoming), "Insulation Installation" (17 incoming), "Roof Structure
Installation" (17 incoming), "Concrete Curing" (12 in / 7 out) in the 384-edge
cluster — are single global nodes referenced by many unrelated element-specific
or building-type-specific sequences (e.g. "Concrete Curing" reused across
columns, beams, and slabs, each with its own locally-valid but
globally-incompatible predecessor/successor). When extraction runs across many
different building contexts, each context's locally-true ordering gets asserted
against the same shared node, and the union inevitably contains contradictions
that are not real domain errors — they're an artifact of missing context scoping.

Confirmed no simple fix applies: restricting to hard_constraint=True edges only
still leaves a 135-198 node cycle (not just soft-preference noise), and none of
the 408 edges have the "self-admitted wrong" rationale signal that resolved the
easy cases. A graph-topology-only feedback-arc-set (Eades heuristic) would need
to deprecate ~80 edges with no correctness signal beyond graph shape — that
risks silently discarding true domain knowledge that only collided because it
shares a canonical node with an unrelated context.

Separately, even a correct resolution wouldn't be durable under the current
design: bsos validate --conflicts (conflict_detection._run_cycle_detection)
re-derives SCCs from live graph state every run. There is no persisted
"reviewed, don't re-flag" state for cycle-shaped conflicts (unlike Sub-task 1's
conflict_pairs, which does persist a classification) — so even a good-faith
manual resolution today will be re-flagged conflicted the next time validate
runs, unless the underlying edges actually change.

Needs (in order):
1. Design how process_relations can express context/variant-scoped orderings
   (e.g. an optional applies_to / building_type / system column, or splitting
   generic hub activities into per-context variants) so extraction doesn't
   keep asserting mutually exclusive orderings onto one shared node.
2. Give cycle detection a durable resolution state so a reviewed cycle isn't
   re-flagged on every validate run when nothing about the edges changed.

Until this lands, the 408 edges in building_domain-g3r's remaining 4 groups
are intentionally left status='conflicted' rather than force-accepted, since
accepting them wouldn't be durable and wouldn't reflect genuine review.
close_reason: Added subject_id column to process_relations (nullable, indexed; migration e2f518508db5) recording which entity's Pass 5 call produced each ordering edge — reusing the existing patterns/antipatterns.subject_id convention. pass5.py sets it going forward; backfill_subject_id() (exposed as 'bsos curate backfill-process-context') recovers it for existing rows by parsing the deterministic PROMPT_TEMPLATE prefix out of source_prompt (100% resolved on production db, 21609/21609 rows). conflict_detection._run_cycle_detection now computes SCCs per subject_id partition (each context's edges + subject_id=NULL 'universal' edges) instead of one global graph, so cross-context reversed-direction edges no longer collide into false cycles. Durable resolution: a cycle's edge-id-set hash is checked against ReviewDecisionRow(item_type='process_relation_cycle') before re-flagging, so a human 'keep-all' decision (review.py _review_cycles) now survives re-runs — this closes the 5ut-style durability gap. Verified end-to-end against production bsos.db: of the 408 edges g3r left conflicted, 400 resolved to non-conflicted (proposed) after re-partitioning; only 8 edges across 4 small same-subject reversed-direction cycles remain, structurally identical to the 24 edges g3r already resolved by hand. title: Resolve 432 process_relations stuck conflicted from cycle detection (16 SCCs)

process_relation, grouped by strongly-connected component) and the doctor
check that flags them, but did not resolve any of the 432 stuck edges
themselves — each cycle needs domain judgement about which edge(s) to break,
which is out of scope for a tooling fix.

Confirmed via bsos review pending --type process_relation --stats: 432 edges
across 16 cycles in production bsos.db, all source_model='deepseek-chat'.

Work:

  at a time. For each of the 16 groups: inspect the edges (predecessor ->
  successor, hard_constraint, rationale), decide which link(s) are actually
  wrong (the ones creating the loop) and break=<indices> to deprecate them
  while accepting the rest, or keep-all if the cycle is a false positive
  (e.g. a legitimately bidirectional/iterative process the extractor
  shouldn't have modeled as strict predecessor/successor), or deprecate-all

- After the session, regenerate and push the process_relations snapshot

    bsos export --format json --type process_relations --output data/snapshot/
    git add data/snapshot/ && git commit -m "snapshot: resolve N cycle conflicts (8lp follow-up)" && git push
- Re-run `bsos doctor` afterward to confirm the cycle-conflict check clears
  (or drops to whatever's left after keep-all/defer decisions).

title: conflict-detection LLM classifier has false-positive 'contradictory' calls on unrelated entity pairs
description: While curating the conflicted-item queue via 'bsos review pending --type conflict' (building_domain-9nw), found real examples where the classifier flagged two assertions as 'contradictory' when they are about entirely different subject/object entity pairs sharing only the same predicate (e.g. 'IfcBoundaryNodeConditionWarping connects_to IfcStructuralPointConnection' vs 'IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity connects_to IfcStructuralItem' — no logical overlap at all, both true). This looks like the embedding similarity pre-filter (SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD=0.80 in conflict_detection.py) is pulling in pairs that are topically close (same predicate, structural-analysis domain) but not actually about the same claim, and the LLM classification prompt (_classify_pair) doesn't push back hard enough on 'contradictory' when subject/object differ entirely. Affects queue quality: real assertion 49207cb2-7676-4245-ac62-989f4ce94ba1 was manually corrected after being wrongly deprecated during review because the review tool assumed every contradictory pair has a right/wrong side (since fixed by adding a 'keep-both / not actually contradictory' action to bsos review pending --type conflict). Worth: (1) tightening the classification prompt to require actual subject/object overlap before allowing 'contradictory', and/or (2) reviewing existing conflict_pairs rows for this pattern to bulk-correct false positives instead of relying on manual per-pair review.
notes: Round 3 (26c21fd): broadened the deterministic rule from 'same subject+predicate' to 'same entity pair (any direction)' — catches chain-shape false positives (same subject, different predicate AND object) that the round-2 rule missed. Resweep confirmed: 33 assertions -> 14 conflicted after round 2's fix; of the 8 newly-classified pairs, 6 were genuine recurring reversed-direction schema errors (not classifier noise) and 2 were the new chain shape. Manually resolved the 6 genuine pairs using IFC4 schema knowledge (d7b9f22) and reset the 2 chain false positives, which cleared instantly under the broadened rule. Conflicted assertion queue is now 0. Remaining open item in this issue's original scope: process_relations (432 items) use a separate deterministic divergence check with no LLM classification, entirely unaffected by any of this — not addressed here.

title: Conflict detection sweep is impractically slow (unbatched CPU embed + sequential LLM calls)
description:
'bsos validate conflicts' (src/bsos/normalization/conflict_detection.py) cannot realistically complete a full sweep over the ~20,732 unevaluated assertions.

Measured during a --limit 20 --model deepseek-chat sample run (building_domain-tzq, 2026-07-05 18:38-20:30, ~111 min total):

- The SentenceTransformer.encode() call over ALL proposed/accepted assertion texts (conflict_detection.py:578, show_progress_bar=False) runs unbatched on CPU and took ~90-100 of the 111 minutes by itself. This cost is paid in full regardless of --limit, since --limit only bounds LLM classification calls (_run_conflict_detection, conflict_detection.py:203-236), not the embedding step. Confirmed via py-spy dump: process was still inside sentence_transformers encode()/torch forward() after 68+ minutes.
- Only 20 LLM calls were needed to evaluate 36 items (~0.56 calls/item at the 0.80 cosine similarity threshold). Extrapolated across the remaining ~20,696 unevaluated assertions at the observed ~18s/item average pace, a full assertion-only sweep would take on the order of 100+ hours (~4+ days) - and that's before constraints/patterns (each with their own embedding pass) are even reached.
- LLM classification calls are fully sequential (one provider.extract() call at a time, no concurrency), which combined with unbatched embedding makes the command impractical to run to completion as currently implemented.

Fixes to consider:
- Batch the encode() call (sentence-transformers supports batch_size) and/or restore a progress bar / periodic log lines so progress is observable.
- Cache/persist assertion embeddings across runs (similar to how pass2/pass10 handle embeddings) instead of recomputing the full set on every invocation.
- Parallelize LLM classification calls (bounded worker pool) similar to the extraction pipeline's --workers pattern.
- Consider a higher/adaptive similarity threshold or pre-clustering to cut candidate pair volume before hitting the LLM.

This blocks building_domain-tzq from being run to full completion; --limit sampling works today but a true full sweep needs this performance work first.
close_reason: Fixed: persistent embedding cache (embeddings table) avoids recomputing ~20k assertion embeddings every run; ThreadPoolExecutor bounded by new --workers flag (default 4) parallelizes LLM classification calls (network I/O only, DB writes stay sequential); encode() now batched (batch_size=64) with progress bar restored. Added regression tests for cache reuse and call concurrency.

title: Bound/control Pass 5 inline activity creation (19k activities from one run)
description:
Pass 5 (_get_or_create_activity) mints a new activity EntityRow for any predecessor/successor name the LLM returns that doesn't already exist, with no bound. In the DeepSeek run this exploded the graph from ~9.9k to 26.9k entities (19,213 activities), inflated passes 6/7 (forcing the zu4 scoping), and drove the lock contention in building_domain-cc0. A from-scratch run would reproduce this.

This is a PREVENTIVE item for the clean-by-construction epic (building_domain-27w): decide what the correct behaviour is and enforce it. Options to evaluate: (a) only create an activity if it matches/normalises to an existing entity, else record as a pending ref rather than minting (mirrors how other passes handle unresolved object names); (b) cap/curate inline activities against a seed activity taxonomy; (c) mark inline-created activities with a distinct status/source so they are clearly second-class and excluded from passes where they add noise. Whatever is chosen, the result must be that a documented from-scratch run does not balloon the graph with thousands of unvetted micro-activities.
notes:
EVIDENCE-BASED REASSESSMENT (2026-06-26, after the full DeepSeek run): recommend NOT implementing the Pass 5 bound as framed; it would destroy value. Inspected the 19,213 activities: the overwhelming majority are legitimate construction-sequencing activities (Electrical Rough-In, Window Waterproofing/Flashing Installation, Formwork & Reinforcement Placement, Drainage/Stormwater Pipe Installation, Final Commissioning) — i.e. exactly the knowledge BSOS exists to capture. 19,061 of 19,213 (99.2%) participate in >=1 process_relation, so they are load-bearing sequencing nodes, not phantom noise.

The downstream harms originally cited are already neutralised: passes 6/7 were scoped off activities (zu4) and the stale pre-scope activity constraints were deleted (cst, done 2026-06-25). Lock contention (cc0) is a perf concern, not data quality.

The ONLY real noise is domain DRIFT: a small minority (~114 matched on furniture/object keywords; order hundreds at most) are object-manufacturing activities (Paintbrush Assembly, Seat Cushion Foam Molding, Cut Headboard Lumber, Compost Pile Formation). Root cause is the ENTITY BOOTSTRAP including non-building objects (chairs, paintbrushes, paintbrushes), not Pass 5. RECOMMENDATION: re-scope this issue (or supersede) to 'entity bootstrap should not seed non-building objects' and keep Pass 5's get_or_create behaviour. Graph size alone is not a defect.

title: Seed ifc_class entities from the authoritative IFC schema; stop LLM-bootstrapping IFC classes
description:
ROOT-CAUSE fix for the recurring IFC junk that building_domain-4se cleans up reactively. Today ifc_class entities are invented by the LLM (Pass 1 bootstrap and Pass 12), which produces hallucinated class names ('IfcHydronicHeatingSystem', 'IfcHotel') and prose pseudo-classes ('IFC Mechanical Equipment', 'IFC Flow Distribution System', 'IFC Animal Facility Space'). The ifc_class table is 682 rows of mixed valid/invalid. Purging after the fact (4se) has to be repeated after every extraction because the LLM keeps re-inventing names from training data.

PROPOSAL: make the ifc_class layer canonical-by-construction. Seed it deterministically from the IFC schema instead of from the LLM:
- Enumerate valid IFC entity/type names from the schema via ifcopenshell (ifcopenshell.ifcopenshell_wrapper.schema_by_name('IFC4'/'IFC4X3').declarations()) or the ifc MCP server's ifc_schema tool. Cover the schema version(s) the project targets (IFC4 minimum; _test.ifc is IFC4).
- Create one ifc_class EntityRow per real IFC entity with the canonical name (and ideally the schema description/supertype as metadata), marked with a deterministic source (e.g. source_model='ifc-schema') so they are distinguishable and never purged by 4se.
- Stop Pass 1/Pass 12 from minting new ifc_class entities by free-text: either drop ifc_class from the LLM concept-discovery output, or constrain Pass 12 to map only to the pre-seeded canonical set (reject/abstain when no real class matches, rather than inventing one).

OUTCOME: ifc_class entities always correspond to real IFC types; get_ifc_psets and scripts/ifc_compliance_report.py get a reliable mapping target; 4se becomes a one-time historical cleanup rather than a recurring chore.

title: Prompts elicit quota-padded output (DeepSeek returns exactly 8 patterns); add quality-over-quantity guidance
description:
Pass 8 writes exactly 8 patterns for the overwhelming majority of entities (live DB: 884 entities with exactly 8 patterns vs 27 with 3-7). This is not a code/schema cap -- PatternExtractionResponse.patterns is an unbounded list and the prompt requests no count. It is DeepSeek V3's output bias: given an open-ended 'list the patterns' prompt with a per-item schema, it settles on a round number (8). The result is patterns padded to an implicit quota rather than a count reflecting how many genuinely apply -- e.g. a Wet Pipe Sprinkler System getting 8 'Alexander-style spatial patterns' when few real ones exist. Quality is uneven; several per entity are likely filler.

The same open-ended 'list all X' framing exists in pass 6 (constraints), pass 7 (anti-patterns), and pass 9 (forces) and very likely produces the same quota-padding there. Worth checking each distribution.

CHANGE: add explicit quality-over-quantity guidance to the pass 6/7/8/9 prompt templates, e.g. 'Only include items that genuinely and specifically apply to this entity. Quality matters far more than quantity -- it is correct to return few items, or none, when the entity is not rich in this dimension. Do not pad the list to reach a count.'

CAVEATS: (1) prompt change busts the LLM cache for the affected pass (new prompt = new cache key) -> re-extraction cost on re-run; (2) only affects not-yet-processed entities, so this is a next-run improvement, not a hot-swap into the current job. Sequence it for after the current run, or for a clean re-run of the affected passes.
notes: REFINED FRAMING (2026-06-22, after inspecting Wet Pipe Sprinkler System's 8 patterns): the quota-padding does NOT produce garbage -- the patterns are genuine, specific, NFPA-flavored design patterns. The padding manifests as REDUNDANCY: when the model runs out of distinct patterns it SUBDIVIDES one into variants to reach 8. Concrete example: 'Grid-Integrated Sprinkler Head Layout', 'Sprinkler Head Alignment with Architectural Grid', and 'Concealed Piping above Accessible Ceiling' are essentially one pattern (coordinate sprinkler heads with the ceiling/structural grid) split three ways. So the real win of the prompt change is DEDUPLICATION, not 'fewer bad patterns'. Prompt guidance should explicitly say: do not split a single pattern into near-duplicate variants to reach a count; merge overlapping patterns into one. Also note: pass 9's related_pattern_ids resolution may already flag some of these as near-duplicates -- check whether that pass can be leveraged to collapse them post-hoc instead of (or in addition to) the prompt change. Original evidence (884 entities at exactly 8) still stands.
close_reason: Added shared QUALITY_GUIDANCE (in bsos.pipeline.__init__) appended to pass 6/7/8/9 prompt templates: instructs models to include only genuinely-applicable items, return few/none when appropriate, and not split one item into near-duplicate variants. Committed 531e775. 458 tests pass. Caveat (already noted): prompt change busts the per-pass LLM cache, so it only affects a future re-extraction, not the current DB's already-processed entities.

title: Purge hallucinated IFC class names from the entity graph
description:
The ifc_class entities contain hallucinated IFC type names that do not exist in any IFC schema. Confirmed example: 'IfcHydronicHeatingSystem' (no such IFC entity). Others are clearly invented too, e.g. 'IFC Class: IfcHotel' (no IfcHotel). The names are also malformed/inconsistent: some are bare ('IfcHydronicHeatingSystem'), some wrapped in prose ('IFC Class: IfcBoiler', 'IFC Beam (IfcBeam)', 'IFC Class IfcDoor (Shop Entrance)'). 390 ifc_class entities total (status != merged), many invalid.

TASK:
1. Build the authoritative list of valid IFC entity/type names. Source it from the IFC schema rather than the LLM — e.g. ifcopenshell (ifcopenshell.ifcopenshell_wrapper.schema_by_name('IFC4'/'IFC4X3').declarations()) or the ifc MCP server's ifc_schema tool. Cover the schema version(s) the project targets (IFC4 at minimum; the test model _test.ifc is IFC4).
2. For each ifc_class entity: extract the candidate Ifc* token from the (often prose-wrapped) name and check it against the valid set, case-sensitively on the canonical IFC capitalisation.
3. Purge or quarantine the hallucinated ones: delete the entity rows AND their dependent assertions/constraints/spatial_relations/process_relations, or set status to a new 'invalid'/'rejected' value so they are excluded from MCP queries. Decide delete vs quarantine (quarantine is safer/auditable).
4. Normalise the surviving valid ones to canonical names (strip the 'IFC Class:' prose wrappers) so they match real IFC class names exactly — this is what get_ifc_psets and the compliance report rely on.

WHY: BSOS maps bsos entities to IFC (get_ifc_psets, scripts/ifc_compliance_report.py). Hallucinated IFC class names break that mapping and mislead any agent that trusts them as real IFC types.
notes:
PARTIAL DONE (2026-06-25, post-DeepSeek run): Built authoritative valid set from ifcopenshell IFC4+IFC4X3 declarations (1173+1311 names). Matcher handles contiguous Ifc-tokens (case-insensitive, so 'IFCReinforcingBar' matches), prose forms ('IFC Door'->IfcDoor, 'IFC Building Storey'->IfcBuildingStorey), and 'IFC Class:' wrappers; drops trailing noise words (class/element/type). Triage of 688 active ifc_class entities: 596 VALID, 92 INVALID. Deprecated (status='deprecated', the codebase convention used by purge.py/doctor.py) the 92 invalid + dependents: 226 assertions, 340 constraints, 479 antipatterns. Invalid set = hallucinated (IfcHotel/IfcOffice/IfcSwimmingPool), non-classes (IfcShaft/IfcSpaceBoundary/IfcPipingSystem), IFC2x3-only names dropped in IFC4 (IfcCalendarDate/IfcAxisPlacement2D/IfcFurnitureElement), and prose (Tiled Floor (Finished)).

REMAINING (step 4 — normalise valid->canonical + DEDUP): the 596 valid entities normalise to only 359 distinct canonical names; e.g. 59 entities -> IfcSpace, 18 -> IfcCovering, 17 -> IfcWall (qualifiers like '(Lift Shaft)'). Renaming in place would create 59 duplicate 'IfcSpace' entities and break name-based lookup (get_ifc_psets). Proper fix = merge duplicates into one canonical entity per class, repointing dependents across ALL tables. NOTE: the existing merge helper (pass2._merge_cluster) only repoints assertions, NOT constraints/antipatterns/forces — so a broader merge is needed. This work is the same as building_domain-y30 (canonical-by-construction); do it there. Triage scripts: scratchpad/triage_ifc2.py + apply_ifc.py.
close_reason: Remaining step-4 (normalise valid prose ifc_class -> canonical + dedup) was delegated to y30/v16/q6y and is now complete: 185 prose entities merged into canonical seeds, hallucinated/non-class names deprecated. The root-cause seeder (y30) makes this a one-time cleanup as intended.

title: Add paraphrase-apl command to rewrite apl_patterns.json in-place
description:
We want the paraphrased prose to live in the repo (data/apl_patterns.json) rather than only being applied at import time. This makes the paraphrased text auditable in version control and keeps import-apl simple (no --model flag needed).

## What to build

Add a `bsos curate paraphrase-apl` command that:
- Reads data/apl_patterns.json
- For each entry without `"paraphrased": true`, calls the LLM to rewrite problem/solution
- Sets `"paraphrased": true` on the entry after rewriting
- Writes back to the JSON file after each pattern (so progress is saved on crash)
- Uses the existing LLM cache in bsos_cache.db for cost-free resumption

The `paraphrased` field prevents drift from multiple paraphrase passes.

## Acceptance criteria
- Running the command twice does not re-paraphrase already-paraphrased entries
- The JSON file after the run has `"paraphrased": true` on every entry
- import-apl without --model imports the already-paraphrased prose correctly

title: Package bsos.db as shared-data in the wheel
description:
The shipped bsos.db (and NOTICE, DATABASE_LICENSE) need to be installed alongside the Python package so users get a working database on 'pip install bsos'.

## What to do

1. Add `platformdirs` to pyproject.toml dependencies.
2. Add `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.shared-data]` entries mapping bsos.db, NOTICE, and DATABASE_LICENSE to share/bsos/.
3. Update `resolve_db_path()` in db_context.py to fall back (after --db / BSOS_DB / .bsos_config) to:

title: Re-paraphrase APL pattern prose for shipped bsos.db
description:
The patterns table in bsos.db is populated by bsos curate apl-import, which copies problem/solution text verbatim from data/apl_patterns.json. The re-paraphrase should:
- Preserve the meaning and intent of each pattern accurately (patterns are central to the tool)
- Be clearly the tool's own expression, not traceable to the book's wording
- Use claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 for cost efficiency (same as the extraction pipeline)

The shipped bsos.db contains no text derived from the book, only:
- Pattern names / ids / graph (fair use / factual)
- LLM-generated prose created by this tool's own pipeline
- LLM-generated assertions from passes 1-12

This allows bsos.db to be licensed under ODbL 1.0 with attribution notices (tracked separately).

4. AbstractionNode cascade (Section 10.3):

title: Pass 10c: Abstraction synthesis
description:
Implement Pass 10c — Section 8.4 abstraction synthesis (the semantic compression system, Section 9).

Algorithm:
1. Group accepted/proposed assertions by subject_id. Within each group, embed assertion texts (all-mpnet-base-v2) and cluster semantically similar ones. Only clusters with ≥ min_cluster_size (default 3) proceed.
2. For each qualifying cluster: ask LLM-A 'what single statement captures all of these without introducing new information?'
3. Adversarial validation via LLM-B (must be different from LLM-A): 'does this abstraction assert anything not already present in these source assertions?' If LLM-B unavailable or same as LLM-A: skip automated validation, set status='proposed'.
4. Create AbstractionNode with status='proposed', child_ids pointing to source assertions. Check 200-node queue cap (Section 4.8) — if exceeded, log warning and stop.
5. Store aggregates edges in graph layer (for later).

AbstractionNode persistence goes through AbstractionNodeRepository (from Phase 3 persistence issue).
Track completion in pass_progress table with key '10c'.

Implementation location: src/bsos/normalization/pass10c.py

title: Pass 10b: Predicate stabilization
description:
Implement Pass 10b — Section 8.3 predicate stabilization.

Two-phase algorithm:
Phase 1 — embedding-based auto-mapping: for each non-core predicate in extracted assertions, compute cosine similarity against all CORE_PREDICATES names (all-mpnet-base-v2). If best match ≥ 0.85: auto-map and update assertions. If [0.60, 0.85): proceed to Phase 2. If < 0.60: write to pending_predicates.

Phase 2 — LLM disambiguation for ambiguous predicates: single LLM classification call per predicate. Provider: first model in --models list (or default_llm_model if running via bsos normalize standalone). Mapped predicates update all assertions and are logged to predicate_mappings table. Unmapped go to pending_predicates (increment occurrence_count if already exists).

Record all mappings in predicate_mappings (original, canonical, method, mapped_at). Check before writing pending predicate to avoid duplicates (deduplication per Section 8.3).
Track completion in pass_progress table with key '10b'.

Implementation location: src/bsos/normalization/pass10b.py

title: Pass 10a: Force/pattern/entity ref resolution
description:
Implement Pass 10a — the first sub-pass of Pass 10 (Section 6, Pass 10 step 1).

Resolves all pending free-text references left by Passes 8 and 9:
1. Pattern.force_descriptions → Force records (exact name match first, then cosine similarity ≥ 0.85 via all-mpnet-base-v2). Matched descriptions move to force_ids; unresolved go to pending_force_refs, then force_descriptions is cleared.
2. Pattern.related_pattern_names → Pattern records (same two-step match). Matched names move to related_pattern_ids; unresolved go to pending_pattern_refs, then related_pattern_names is cleared.
3. Force.affects entity names → Entity UUIDs (exact match only per spec, no similarity search). Unresolved go to pending_entity_refs.

Per-item atomicity: each pattern/force processed in its own DB transaction so the step is resumable (Section 6 Pass 10).
On completion write config key passes_3_9_refs_resolved = '1'.

title: Phase 2 MCP query tools: constraints, failure modes, patterns, forces, spatial, process sequence
description:
Extend the MCP server with all Phase 2 query tools (PROPOSAL.md Section 13.3).

New tools to add to bsos/mcp_server/server.py:

1. get_constraints(entity) → list[ConstraintResult]
   - Constraint records where subject_id matches entity (via resolve_entity)
   - Returns: rule, constraint_type, conditions, exceptions, confidence, knowledge_origin, status
   - Sort: confidence DESC then knowledge_origin priority (physical > engineering > architectural > cultural)

2. get_failure_modes(entity) → list[AntiPatternResult]
   - AntiPattern records where subject_id matches entity
   - Returns: name, conditions, consequences, mitigations, confidence, knowledge_origin, status

3. get_patterns(entity) → list[PatternResult]
   - Pattern records where subject_id matches entity
   - PatternResult.forces: populated from force_ids resolved to Force names; if force_ids empty and force_descriptions non-empty, use raw descriptions with a warning in the result
   - Returns: name, problem, solution, context, forces, consequences, emergent_properties, confidence, knowledge_origin, status

4. get_forces(entity) → list[ForceResult]
   - Force records where entity UUID appears in affects JSON array
   - Returns: name, direction, confidence, knowledge_origin, rationale, status

5. get_spatial_relations(entity) → list[SpatialRelationResult]
   - SpatialRelation records where subject_id OR object_id matches entity
   - Returns: subject (resolved name), relation, object (resolved name), confidence, knowledge_origin, status

6. get_process_sequence(entity, max_depth=50) → ProcessSequenceResult
   - Build local NetworkX DiGraph from ProcessRelation rows (predecessor→successor edges)
   - BFS/DFS from entity in both directions up to max_depth hops to find reachable subgraph
   - MUST call nx.is_directed_acyclic_graph; if cycle detected return has_cycle=True with partial sequence and cycle_description
   - If DAG: return nx.topological_sort result as sequence (entity names, predecessors first)
   - truncated=True if max_depth reached before exhausting graph

All tools MUST:
- Use resolve_entity (case-insensitive, alias-aware, skips merged)
- Return {'error': 'entity_not_found', ...} dict on unknown entity (not raise)
- Each create their own session (concurrency safe)
- Support min_confidence, max_results, include_proposed shared params (Section 13.1)

Update create_server() to register all new tools.
Tests: tests/integration/test_mcp_server_phase2.py covering each tool with fixture data; get_process_sequence DAG ordering test, cycle detection test.

title: Entity bootstrap seeds non-building objects, causing activity domain drift
description:
The Pass 1 entity bootstrap seeds non-building objects (chairs, paintbrushes, headboards, cushions) as entities. Pass 5 then correctly generates manufacturing sequences for them, producing out-of-domain activities like 'Paintbrush Assembly', 'Seat Cushion Foam Molding', 'Cut Headboard Lumber', 'Compost Pile Formation'. In the full DeepSeek run ~hundreds of the 19,213 activities (~114 matched on obvious furniture/object keywords) are this drift.

ROOT CAUSE is upstream in the entity bootstrap (concept discovery), NOT Pass 5 — Pass 5 is doing its job. This supersedes the framing of building_domain-yms, which proposed bounding Pass 5; evidence shows the 19k activities are overwhelmingly legitimate construction sequencing (99.2% carry process_relations) and bounding Pass 5 would destroy value.

TASK: constrain the Pass 1 concept-discovery prompt (and/or a post-filter) so it does not emit furnishable/manufacturable objects as first-class building entities — or scope them so Pass 5 does not generate their manufacturing sequences. Preventive item for the clean-by-construction epic (building_domain-27w). Measure the drift precisely first (keyword + LLM classification) before deciding delete vs prevent.
notes:
PREVENTIVE FIX LANDED (fa02c1c, 2026-06-26): added SCOPE_NOTE to all three Pass 1 concept-discovery prompts (BOOTSTRAP, DOMAIN, EXPANSION). Keeps building fabric/systems/spaces/materials + fixed/building-integrated FF&E (IfcFurniture is legitimately modelled); excludes loose consumer goods, personal/gardening/composting items, tableware, toys; and restricts activities to on-site construction/installation/commissioning, never off-site manufacture. 458 tests pass. Caveat: prompt change busts the Pass 1 LLM cache, so it only takes effect on a future re-run — UNVERIFIED until then.

DRIFT MEASUREMENT (current DB): the boundary is genuinely fuzzy. A broad keyword sweep (chair/seat/bench/bed/table/desk/etc.) over component/material/system entities is dominated by false positives — building fabric ('Mortar Bed','Bed Joint','Chair Rail','Road Bed','Window Seat','Lamp Post') and building-integrated FF&E ('Auditorium Seat','Grandstand Seating','Reception Desk') that IFC models. The clearly-out-of-scope core is small: Paintbrush, Compost Bin/Tumbler/Screening, Worm Farm, Keepsake Storage Box, loose Armchair/Gaming/Rocking/Recliner Chair, Sofa, Coffee/Side Table, Mattress, Headboard. In activities, ~114/19,213 (0.6%) matched furniture/object keywords.

REACTIVE DELETION: DEFERRED as low-value/high-risk. The drift is <1% of activities and low-harm (a stray 'Paintbrush Assembly' won't mislead construction sequencing), while precise classification needs an LLM pass (API cost) and blanket keyword deletion would wrongly remove legit FF&E. Proper remedy = the preventive prompt fix + a clean re-run, per the clean-by-construction philosophy (epic 27w). Reopen the reactive angle only if a specific consumer demands a pruned current DB.
close_reason: Preventive fix landed (fa02c1c): SCOPE_NOTE added to all three Pass 1 concept-discovery prompts to keep concepts within the built environment and restrict activities to on-site construction (not off-site manufacture). 458 tests pass. Reactive deletion of current-DB drift deferred as low-value/high-risk (<1% of activities, fuzzy boundary vs legit IFC furniture); remedy is the prompt fix + a clean re-run per epic 27w. Like 8tk, takes effect on next run.

title: Pass 5+ writers occasionally hit 'database is locked' under 2 workers
description:
During long DeepSeek extraction runs, pass5 (and likely passes 4/6-9 with the same pattern) occasionally log 'pass5_entity_error ... (sqlite3.OperationalError) database is locked' when inserting an inline activity entity (_get_or_create_activity -> session.flush, pass5.py:79).

ROOT CAUSE: WAL allows one writer at a time. Each _process_entity holds the write lock across many ops in a single transaction (flush per new activity + dedup SELECT + flush per relation). With 2 workers contending plus occasional WAL checkpoint stalls, a blocked writer can exceed the 30s busy_timeout (database.py:32) and error.

IMPACT: benign + recoverable. The exception fires before session.commit() (pass5.py:198), so the transaction rolls back and no PassProgressRow(status=completed) is written -> the entity is reprocessed free (LLM cached) on the next run. No corruption, no data loss. Re-running the same extract command backfills skipped entities at no API cost.

POSSIBLE FIXES (pick one, all low-risk): (1) retry the per-entity transaction on OperationalError 'database is locked' with short backoff; (2) shorten the write-transaction hold time by committing inline activity creation in its own short transaction before the relation loop; (3) raise busy_timeout to 60000. Option 1 or 2 preferred over just bumping the timeout.
notes: Observed 2026-06-19 during the deepseek-chat full extraction run (building_domain-efo). Example: entity 'Balcony Tile / Decking Installation' failed inserting 'Balcony Waterproofing / Membrane'.
close_reason: Added with_db_retry helper (src/bsos/persistence/retry.py): retries the full per-entity worker on SQLite 'database is locked' with exponential backoff+jitter. Wired into passes 4-9 via pool.submit(with_db_retry, _process_entity, ...). Safe because each worker owns its transaction (rolls back on error) and LLM calls are cached. Non-lock errors propagate immediately. Tests in tests/unit/test_db_retry.py.

title: Review 1,478 completely isolated entities
description: 1,478 entities have no assertions as subject or object — they appear in neither direction of any relationship. Examples: Frosted Glass, Nuclear Density Testing, Household Mix, Timber Seat Framing. Some are legitimate leaf concepts; others look like pass 1 over-extraction. Review a sample and decide: (a) deprecate/reject the clearly spurious ones, (b) accept the rest as valid vocabulary even without relationships. Query: sqlite3 bsos.db "SELECT e.name, e.entity_type FROM entities e WHERE e.status='proposed' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM assertions a WHERE a.subject_id=e.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM assertions a WHERE a.object_id=e.id) ORDER BY entity_type, name;"
notes:
REVIEWED 2026-06-28. Isolated count grew 1,478 -> 18,544 since filing (DB expanded). Breakdown of isolated proposed: activity 17,357 | component 446 | material 298 | ifc_class 174 | system 162 | space 107.

DECISIONS:
- activity/material/component/system (~18,260): overwhelmingly legitimate leaf vocabulary (e.g. 'Site Excavation and Leveling', 'Breathable Membrane', 'Cantilever Beam', 'Air Curtain'). NOT over-extraction. Kept proposed for promotion task building_domain-lfy. Activities dominate because process-sequence passes simply haven't linked them yet, not because they're spurious.
- space: deprecated 17 type-mismatched, name-only entities (A Pattern Language social/regional/material abstractions miscast as 'space': Men And Women, Household Mix, Community Of 7000, Children In The City, Mosaic Of Subcultures, Subculture Boundary, City Country Fingers, Lace Of Country Streets, The Distribution Of Towns, Polycentric Metropolitan Region, Good Materials, Ornament, Warm Colors, Efficient Structure, Lapped Outside Walls, Dancing In The Street, Small Services Without Red Tape). 16/17 had empty descriptions. title: Compliance report: per-space MEP checks via space boundaries
description:
The compliance report currently checks MEP system presence building-wide (any IfcSanitaryTerminal anywhere in the model). This produces false passes: a building with one toilet could show Drainage System PASS for every kitchen.

The correct check is whether the space itself has a relevant fixture in its space boundaries (space.BoundedBy → RelatedBuildingElement). For example, a kitchen with an IfcSanitaryTerminal bounding it has drainage; one without doesn't. IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel records are already present in _test.ifc (213 of them).

Acceptance: the Kitchen drainage check passes only if an IfcSanitaryTerminal appears in that space's BoundedBy relations, not if one exists elsewhere in the model.

title: MCP tool: write-back / propose new assertion
description:
Knowledge flow in bsos is currently one-directional: extracted from text, queried by agents. When an IFC-manipulating agent discovers something true in a real model that bsos does not know (a novel spatial arrangement, a constraint that proves wrong in practice), there is no way to feed that back.

Add a bsos MCP tool (e.g. propose_assertion) that allows an agent to submit a candidate assertion (subject, predicate, object, rationale, confidence) into bsos with status=proposed for human review. This closes the learning loop and allows the knowledge base to grow from model evidence, not just text extraction.

title: Build and verify the knowledge graph

- bsos validate topology: no entrance nodes defined, and on inspection this corpus aggregates entities across many building archetypes rather than one instantiated model — marking entrances doesn't cleanly apply at the corpus level. Not applicable here; would be meaningful when running topology checks against one loaded IFC model via the ifc MCP server, not this general KB.
- bsos validate conflicts --dry-run: scope is 20,732 unevaluated assertions, 0 ProcessRelation divergence candidates. This requires an LLM classification call per candidate, the same order of cost/time as an extraction pass, so per CLAUDE.md convention it needs a correctly-configured provider key in a separate terminal (this session's env had a mismatched/typo'd key setup — see building_domain-tzq). Net: graph build + doctor + ground-truth pattern coverage are done and clean (modulo the filed cosmetic bug). Conflict detection is the one substantive piece of verification still outstanding, tracked in building_domain-tzq.

ifcopenshell create_shape() returns a shape whose .geometry .verts/.faces are buffers owned by the parent shape object. Accessing them via the one-liner 'geom = create_shape(s, elem).geometry' drops the parent immediately, so after gc the .faces index buffer reads back as garbage (indices >> vertex count) and any consumer like ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_footprint_area raises IndexError. FIX: keep the create_shape() result bound (shape = create_shape(...); geom = shape.geometry) for as long as you read its buffers. NOTE: get_footprint_area itself is NOT buggy — it works correctly (and is rotation-invariant) once the shape is kept alive; an earlier note claiming it was buggy was a misdiagnosis of this lifetime issue.
